REQUIREMENT: Avatar Upload
Users can upload one avatar image to their profile.
An uploaded image must be smaller than 2 MB.
Images must be stored securely.
Accept all common image formats.
Replacing an avatar should be easy.

- “one avatar image” could mean one active image per profile, or one upload allowed over the profile’s lifetime.
- “smaller than 2 MB” could mean strictly below 2,000,000 bytes, below 2 MiB, or a UI/API file-size limit measured differently.

- “all common image formats” does not specify the supported MIME types, file extensions, animated-image behavior, or whether formats are converted during processing.
- “Replacing an avatar should be easy” does not specify the user flow, whether replacement is in-place, whether deletion is supported, or what happens if replacement fails.

- What replacement and deletion workflow should the profile UI provide, and should the previous image be removed immediately after a successful replacement?
- Are image dimensions, aspect ratio, file naming, resizing, thumbnail generation, or processing-time limits required?
- What should happen when an upload or replacement fails, and should the existing avatar remain unchanged?

- The size check applies to the uploaded file before any transformation and uses a byte-based limit once defined.
- The system will validate file content rather than relying only on client-provided extensions or MIME types.
- A failed replacement will leave the current avatar intact.
- Avatar access will be limited to authorized profile viewers unless the product specifies public avatars.

The core requirement is clear: support one securely stored, replaceable profile avatar subject to a size limit and common image-format support. Implementation still needs decisions on exact size units, supported formats, security/access controls, and the replacement/deletion experience.

## Confirmed Facts
- Users can download the records shown in a report as a CSV file.
- The export must respect the user’s current filters.
- The export must respect the user’s access permissions.
- The CSV must include a header row containing the column names.
- Large exports should run in the background so the user can continue working.
- The user must be notified when the file is ready.
- Download links must remain available for a reasonable time.
- If an export fails, the system must explain what happened and allow the user to try again.

## Ambiguities
- “records shown in a report” is unclear about whether hidden, paginated, aggregated, or otherwise non-row data is included in the CSV.
- “current filters” does not define which filter state is captured, especially if filters change while an export is queued or running.
- “access permissions” does not specify whether permissions are checked when the export is requested, when it runs, or when the file is downloaded.
- “Large exports” has no threshold or performance definition for when background processing is required.
- “Notify the user” does not specify the notification channel, delivery timing, or behavior if notification delivery fails.
- “A reasonable time” does not define the download-link retention period or whether retention is configurable.
- “Explain what happened” does not define the level of technical detail, user-facing error categories, or handling of sensitive error information.
- “Try again” does not specify whether the retry reuses the original parameters or captures the user’s then-current report state.

## Clarification Questions
- Should exports contain all rows matching the report query, or only rows currently visible on the page, and how should grouped or aggregated reports be represented?
- At what point should the system snapshot filters, report configuration, and permissions: request time, job start, or download time?
- What row-count, file-size, or execution-time threshold determines whether an export runs in the background?
- Which notification mechanisms are required (in-app, email, or both), and what message/statuses should users receive?
- How long should completed download links remain available, and what should happen after they expire?
- What export format details are required, such as character encoding, delimiter, quoting, line endings, null values, and filename convention?
- What failure cases must be exposed to users, and should the system provide an error code or support reference?
- Should retry reuse the original export parameters or use the report’s current filters and permissions?
- Are there limits on concurrent exports, export size, or export frequency, and what should users see when those limits are reached?

## Assumptions
- CSV export is initiated from an existing report and uses the report’s available columns unless clarified otherwise.
- The exported dataset is limited to data the requesting user is authorized to access.
- Background processing applies only when the configured large-export threshold is exceeded; smaller exports may complete synchronously.
- The system stores completed files temporarily and removes or invalidates them after the retention period.
- A failed export does not produce a downloadable partial file.
- The export job records the parameters needed to reproduce the requested report state.

## Summary
The requirement establishes a permission-aware CSV export with headers, asynchronous processing for large jobs, completion notification, temporary download availability, and retryable failure handling. - Users can upload one avatar image to their profile.
- An uploaded image must be smaller than 2 MB.
- Images must be stored securely.
- The system should accept all common image formats.
- Replacing an avatar should be easy.

## Ambiguities
- “one avatar image” — It is unclear whether each user may retain only one active avatar, whether upload history is allowed, and whether an avatar is optional. Decision owner: Product.
- “smaller than 2 MB” — It is unclear whether the limit is strictly less than 2 MB or inclusive of 2 MB, and whether MB means decimal megabytes or binary mebibytes. Decision owner: Product/Engineering.
- “stored securely” — It does not define required encryption, access controls, isolation, retention, malware scanning, or compliance requirements. Decision owner: Security/Compliance.
- “all common image formats” — The supported format list, MIME/signature validation rules, and handling of animated or oversized images are unspecified. Decision owner: Product/Engineering/Security.
- “Replacing an avatar should be easy” — The expected user flow, permissions, overwrite behavior, and whether replacement is immediate are not defined. Decision owner: Product/UX.

## Clarification Questions
- Should users have exactly one active avatar, and may they remove it or retain prior versions? Decision owner: Product.
- Does “smaller than 2 MB” mean strictly under 2,000,000 bytes, under 2 MiB, or another threshold? Decision owner: Product/Engineering.
- Which image formats must be supported, and should the system normalize, resize, or strip metadata from uploads? Decision owner: Product/Engineering/Security.
- What security controls are mandatory for storage and processing, including encryption at rest/in transit, private access, malware scanning, and retention/deletion? Decision owner: Security/Compliance.
- What should happen when a user uploads a replacement: replace immediately, preserve the old image temporarily, and allow cancellation or recovery? Decision owner: Product/UX.
- Who can view or change an avatar, and are there moderation, privacy, or authorization requirements? Decision owner: Product/Security.

## Assumptions
- Each user has at most one active avatar visible on their profile.
- Uploading a replacement will make the new image active without requiring a separate administrative action.
- The size limit will be enforced before durable storage, subject to the confirmed byte definition.
- Only valid image files, rather than arbitrary files renamed with image extensions, will be accepted.
- Avatar storage will be private by default and served only through authorized application access.

## Summary
The requirement establishes a single profile-avatar upload capability with a size limit, secure storage, broad image-format support, and straightforward replacement. Product, Engineering, UX, Security, and Compliance must still decide the exact size interpretation, supported formats and processing, security controls, lifecycle behavior, and access rules.

## Confirmed Facts
- Workspace owners can invite someone to join their workspace by email.
- Accepting an invitation adds the person to the workspace as a member.
- Each invitation link can be accepted only once.
- Each invitation expires after seven days.
- Workspace owners can cancel pending invitations.
- Owners can see which invitations are still awaiting a response.
- The system must handle invitations sent to existing members appropriately.
- The system must handle repeated invitations appropriately.

## Ambiguities
- "by email" does not specify whether the invitee must already have an account, whether invitations can be sent to multiple recipients, or what email validation is required. Decision owner: Product, with Security input.
- "adds the person to the workspace as a member" does not define when membership takes effect, whether the invitee must authenticate as the invited email address, or what happens if the invitee belongs to another role or workspace. Decision owner: Product and Security.
- "accepted only once" does not define whether a second acceptance attempt should show an error, redirect to the workspace, or be treated as already completed. Decision owner: Product.
- "expires after seven days" does not define whether expiry is measured from creation or delivery, the exact cutoff and timezone, or whether owners can resend or extend an expired invitation. Decision owner: Product and Engineering.
- "cancel a pending invitation" does not define whether cancellation invalidates an already-issued link immediately, whether cancellation can be reversed, or what status is shown afterward. Decision owner: Product and Security.
- "which invitations are still waiting for a response" does not define the invitation fields, sorting, pagination, visibility, or whether expired and canceled invitations appear. Decision owner: Product and Privacy/Compliance.
- "Handle invitations to existing members ... appropriately" does not specify whether the system should reject, no-op, notify, or replace an existing membership invitation. Decision owner: Product.
- "repeated invitations appropriately" does not define whether duplicates are blocked, merged, resent, rate-limited, or tracked as separate invitations. Decision owner: Product, with Security input.
- The requirement does not specify authorization boundaries, such as whether all workspace owners may invite, whether there are invitation limits, or how abuse is prevented. Decision owner: Product and Security.
- The requirement does not specify the invitation delivery, acceptance, and failure user experiences or notification content. Decision owner: Product and Design.

## Clarification Questions
- Must invitees have an account already, and must acceptance verify access to the invited email address? Decision owner: Product and Security.
- Can an owner invite one email at a time or multiple addresses in one action, and what email formats or domains are allowed? Decision owner: Product.
- From which event is the seven-day expiration calculated, and what timezone/precision defines the cutoff? Decision owner: Product and Engineering.
- What should happen when an expired invitation is opened, and may an owner resend or renew it? Decision owner: Product.
- What should happen when a canceled link is opened, and is cancellation immediately enforced? Decision owner: Product and Security.
- What response should a user receive when accepting an already-used invitation? Decision owner: Product.
- How should invitations to existing members behave: reject, no-op, notify, or create a separate record? Decision owner: Product.
- How should repeated invitations to the same email and workspace behave, including pending, expired, canceled, and accepted states? Decision owner: Product.
- Which invitation statuses and fields should owners see, and should expired/canceled invitations remain visible? Decision owner: Product and Privacy/Compliance.
- Are there invitation quotas, rate limits, audit-log requirements, or abuse controls? Decision owner: Security and Compliance.
- What roles or permissions can the new member receive, and what happens if the invitee already has a different role? Decision owner: Product and Security.
- What email provider, template, sender identity, localization, and delivery/retry behavior are required? Decision owner: Product and Engineering.

## Assumptions
- Only authorized workspace owners can create or cancel invitations for their workspace.
- An invitation is scoped to one workspace and one email address.
- Acceptance requires a secure, unguessable invitation link and associates the resulting membership with the invited email identity.
- A pending invitation is one that has been created, has not been accepted or canceled, and has not expired.
- Membership is created atomically with successful acceptance, and a used link cannot create another membership.
- The initial member role is the workspace's default member role unless Product specifies otherwise.
- Existing-member and duplicate-invitation behavior will be decided before implementation rather than inferred from the status list.
- Invitation events should be auditable, subject to applicable privacy and retention policies.

## Summary
The core flow and lifecycle requirements are clear: owners create email invitations, invitees accept once within seven days, owners can cancel invitations, and pending invitations are visible. Product, Security, Compliance, Design, and Engineering must still define identity verification, duplicate/existing-member behavior, lifecycle cutoff and UI semantics, authorization and abuse controls, and delivery details.
